title: The Learning Hub
before:
The Maine Department of Education (DOE) supports teaching and learning in every content area through the resources below. Each content area links to its instructional resources, the Maine Learning Results (MLRs) — the State's PK-12 educational standards — and its standards review. The department also maintains the Maine Early Learning and Development Standards (MELDS) for early learning and the Guiding Principles for Learning, which describe the cross-disciplinary knowledge, skills, and dispositions all Maine students are expected to develop.

Foundational & Cross-Disciplinary

Standards That Reach Across Every Content Area
  • Maine's Guiding Principles for Learning — the cross-disciplinary knowledge, skills, and dispositions all Maine students are expected to develop.
  • Maine Early Learning & Development Standards (MELDS) — standards for early learning, supporting children from birth through age five.

New to the standards review process? The Maine DOE conducts a scheduled, periodic review of the Maine Learning Results in each content area, bringing together Maine educators and interested parties to evaluate, revise, and strengthen the standards. Learn more at the Standards Review Home.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Draw a closing link as the action it is
decisions.why: 1 passage ends with a paragraph holding nothing but a link — the thing the passage was leading up to. Set as running text it looks like any other link in the sentence above it. The site already has one way of drawing an action, so it takes that. The words do not change.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 2 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
decisions.removes: Content & Standards - The Learning Hub Banner - 6.25.2026.png

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 2 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
